modes.title: Remove Glare
modes.subtitle: Erase reflections and glare from clear eyeglass lenses
modes.prompt: Edit only the reflections on the clear lenses of the eyeglasses in this photo. Remove every reflection, glare, light spot, highlight, sparkle and window, screen, lamp or sky reflection on the lenses so they look clean and see-through, and restore the eyes behind them realistically from what is already partly visible, keeping the person's exact eye shape, eye color, iris and pupil size, gaze direction, eyelids, eyelashes, skin tone and the original lighting. Keep the natural lens tint and the slight optical distortion of the lens. If the lenses are dark sunglasses and the eyes are not visible in the original, do not invent or reveal eyes: keep the lenses dark and only remove the reflected images. Do not modify the glasses frame, nose pads or temples in any way. Do not change the face, facial features, identity, expression, skin, makeup, hair, clothing, body, pose, background, colors, white balance, contrast, sharpness, grain, resolution, aspect ratio, zoom, crop or framing. Do not retouch, beautify, smooth, relight or enhance anything. Everything outside the lens area must remain pixel-identical to the original photo. Output the same photo with only the lens reflections removed.

modes.title: Remove Glasses
modes.subtitle: Take the glasses off entirely, naturally
modes.prompt: Edit only the eyeglasses in this photo. Completely remove the glasses from the person's face, including the frame, lenses, nose pads, hinges and temple arms, and any part of the temples over the ears or hair. Reconstruct the areas that were covered or distorted by the glasses so the person looks exactly as they would without glasses: their real eyes, eyebrows, eyelids, eyelashes, under-eye area, nose bridge, cheeks, temples, ears and hair, with the same identity, eye shape, eye color, gaze direction, skin tone, skin texture and pores, and lighting as the rest of the face. Remove the lens magnification or shrinking effect so the eyes have their natural size and position. Remove nose pad marks, frame shadows and lens reflections. Do not change the face shape, facial features, identity, age, expression, makeup, hair style, clothing, body, pose, background, colors, white balance, contrast, sharpness, grain, resolution, aspect ratio, crop or framing. Do not retouch, beautify, smooth, relight or enhance anything. Everything not covered by the glasses must remain pixel-identical to the original photo. Output the same photo with only the glasses removed.

modes.title: Sunglasses
modes.subtitle: Wipe reflections off dark lenses, keep the tint
modes.prompt: This is a real photo of a person wearing dark sunglasses. Edit only the inside of the two sunglass lenses: remove the reflected images mirrored on them (window, room, person, phone, sky, lights and bright spots). Nothing else in the photo may change. The lenses must stay dark, tinted and opaque, with exactly the same color, hue and darkness as the reflection-free parts of the original lenses. The eyes must stay hidden: do not add, reveal or draw eyes, eyebrows or skin inside the lenses. The lenses must still look like real curved glossy glass photographed in the same light, not a flat painted or matte fill: keep a subtle natural tonal gradient that follows the lens curvature, slightly lighter toward the edges, a soft faint sheen from the ambient light, a very thin subtle highlight along the inner rim, and the same noise, grain, sharpness and compression texture as the rest of the photo. Keep the sunglasses frame exactly as it is: same shape, size, thickness, metal or plastic color, shine, bridge, nose pads, hinges, temples and their position on the face. The lens outline must follow the original frame exactly. Do not change the face, identity, skin, makeup, expression, hair, jewelry, clothing, hands, tattoos, pose, background, colors, white balance, exposure, contrast or lighting. Do not retouch, beautify, smooth, sharpen, upscale, zoom, crop, reframe or change the aspect ratio. Everything outside the two lenses must remain pixel-identical to the original photo. Output the same photo with only the reflections on the sunglass lenses removed.
